messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Create a heat probability density function from scatter plot
parts:
For the first 3 graphs you're dividing your dataset into different colors or different graphs by a factor that your example dataset does not have. 

To do a 2D density plot you could do the following. 

ggplot(x, aes(duration, pitch)) +
  stat_density2d(geom = "tile", aes(fill = ..density..), contour = F) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colour = c("darkblue", "lightblue", "green", "yellow", "orange", "red"), legend=F)

grid.arrange() from gridExtra should allow you to arrange all the plots in a stacked manner, you just need to build each one first and then put them together. 
http://code.google.com/p/gridextra/

There have been posts here recently on aligning plots that should help you get things lined up well. 

Brandon

messages.subject: Re: Create a heat probability density function from scatter plot
parts:
Hi:

There are a few examples of defining one's own color scale on pp. 105
and 106 of the ggplot2 book. AFAIR, Color Brewer scales are generally
discrete (I have a notation that says Brewer color palettes are
designed for use with factors), but the colorspace and vcd packages
allow for continuous gradients in color scales. If you don't have the
book, the code for the examples in question are on the book's web
site:
http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/book/scales.r

Look for the eruptions example somewhere between a third and a half
way into the code; you should see a function for defining continuous
palettes with scale_*_gradientn after package vcd is loaded [vcd loads
colorspace in the process]. The ColorBrewer palette examples follow
shortly thereafter.

HTH,
Dennis
